message.content: {"answer": "D", "option_text": "New opacities have appeared in both lungs, suggesting cryptogenic organizing pneumonia.", "reason": "Visual comparison of the original images shows progression from a unilateral right lower lung opacity (Figure 1a) to bilateral patchy consolidations involving both lungs (Figure 4). The chest_xray_classifier confirmed strong Lung Opacity scores for both timepoints (0.88 and 0.89), supporting the presence of significant disease. This pattern of migrating or expanding bilateral opacities is characteristic of cryptogenic organizing pneumonia (COP), whereas adenocarcinoma in situ typically presents as ground-glass opacity without such rapid consolidation, and resolving pneumonia would show decreased opacity."}
